title: Augmented strict quotient-tower comparison under ordinary qcqs restriction
statement: Fix ell,E and weakly etale s:S->V followed by an immersion i:V->T of qcqs schemes [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Put r=s followed by i and use the fixed ordinary module and complex pullback of [def-fix-qcqs-completion-ordinary-models]. There is a natural isomorphism from the strict quotient tower of P followed termwise by ordinaryComplexPull r to the strict quotient tower of ordinaryComplexPull r, with the tower and augmentation of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For every complex P and every n, applying ordinaryComplexPull to its nth augmentation and then the nth component of the isomorphism equals the nth augmentation of ordinaryComplexPull(P). No Roos or derived comparison is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion, clause (1); Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply; weakly etale slice restriction in Tag 09AE, definition-extension-zero; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.5.8(1). Tensor comparison: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, and 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product.

proof.text: Take the invertibility of ordinaryCoefficientMap for s followed by i from qcqsOrdinaryRestrictionExact. For each positive quotient exponent apply ordinaryQuotientModuleComparison. Its natural isomorphism is between completed-module quotients followed by ordinary pullback and ordinary pullback followed by the quotient. Apply it termwise to complexes; naturality in the module maps proves compatibility with the differentials.

For adjacent exponents compare the two chain maps after the ordinary pullback adjunction. Pure-tensor extensionality reduces their equality to a section a tensor x. Naturality of the adjunction unit moves the quotient transition before the unit. The specified comparison formula and the recorded transition formula reduce the desired square to the constant-section finite ring-map square (proved locally from sheafification-adjunction naturality and evaluated at the finite quotient transition). Thus NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles the maps into a strict tower map. Each component is invertible, so the tower map is invertible; naturality in the original complex is the naturality of each termwise comparison.

Compare the augmentation equation degreewise after the same ordinary adjunction. Naturality of its unit moves the source augmentation before the unit. Both augmentations send x to 1 tensor x; the normalized finite-module comparison sends this to 1 tensor the unit pullback of x, because ordinaryFiniteRingMap preserves one. The defining generator formula for the target augmentation gives the required equality.

lean.statement:
theorem qcqsOrdinaryQuotientRestriction
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {S V T : Scheme.{t}} [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    [CompactSpace V] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V] [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T]
    (s : S ⟶ V) (i : V ⟶ T) [WeaklyEtale s] [IsImmersion i] :
    let r := s ≫ i
    ∃ (τ : tower l E T none ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ (Cx l E T none) (Cx l E S none)).obj
            (ordinaryComplexPull l E r) ≅
          ordinaryComplexPull l E r ⋙ tower l E S none),
        (∀ (P : Cx l E T none) (n : ℕ),
          (ordinaryComplexPull l E r).map (((augmentation l E T none).app P).app (op n)) ≫
              (τ.hom.app P).app (op n) =
            ((augmentation l E S none).app ((ordinaryComplexPull l E r).obj P)).app (op n))
